quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes.
Use the rear brake firmly while gradually increasing the braking pressure of the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Apply both brakes at the same time to stop quickly.

questions.question: The effects of marijuana consumption can last for:

options.text: No more than 15 minutes.
About an hour.
About two hours.
More than six hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: More than six hours.
questions.explanation: When smoked, marijuana affects you within minutes and lasts 2-4 hours. When eaten, it takes over an hour to work but effects can last more than six hours.

questions.question: Which formation is best for a group of riders entering a curve?

options.text: Pyramid
Staggered
Single-file
Compressed

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: Use single-file formation when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway. A staggered formation is better for maintaining close spacing on straight roads.

questions.question: When applying the front brake, you should:

options.text: Apply the lever by squeezing firmly and progressively.
Grab at the brake with only two fingers.
Press down on the brake lever with your foot.
Stomp on the brake lever.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the lever by squeezing firmly and progressively.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the brake lever with all four fingers. Start firmly and gradually apply more pressure.

questions.question: Proper clothing for riding offers all of the following, except:

options.text: Comfort.
Protection in a collision.
Protection from the cold.
Discomfort.

questions.correctAnswerText: Discomfort.
questions.explanation: Proper riding clothes protect you from injury in a crash and from weather. They provide comfort, not discomfort.

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Is discouraged because it can cause heat-related problems.
Should only be done if the jacket is a light color.
Is not important.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants in hot weather. They protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration, along with other safety benefits.

questions.question: Which factor does not play a role in a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
Body weight
How quickly the alcohol was consumed
How often alcohol is consumed

questions.correctAnswerText: How often alcohol is consumed
questions.explanation: Three major factors affect BAC: amount consumed, how quickly you drank it, and body weight. How often you drink does not affect BAC.

questions.question: As weight transfers to the front of your bike while you are braking, you should:

options.text: Gradually increase pressure to the front brake.
Use more rear brake pressure.
Not worry. The weight transfer will not have an effect on your motorcycle.
Try to lock the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gradually increase pressure to the front brake.
questions.explanation: As you brake, the bike's weight moves forward to the front tire. Gradually increase the pressure on the front brake as this happens.

questions.question: If you must swerve, you should:

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn your handlebars quickly.
Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: Apply light pressure to the handgrip in the direction you want to turn. To swerve left, press the left grip, then the right to straighten. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: When both braking and swerving must be done to avoid an unexpected hazard, a rider should:

options.text: Perform one action, then the other.
Perform both actions at the same time and apply extra braking pressure.
Perform both actions at the same time, but mainly focus on swerving.
Not perform either action.

questions.correctAnswerText: Perform one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Do not brake and swerve at the same time because you need full traction to swerve safely. Do one action first, then the other.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Leave the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is dangerous when wet. When it rains, avoid the center by riding in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is often the safest choice.

questions.question: If a passing vehicle creates a wind blast that hits you, where should you ride to have the most room to recover?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the middle of your lane gives you the most space to handle a wind blast from a passing vehicle.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of the lane should you use?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
Either the left or right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you away from opening car doors, people stepping out, and cars pulling into traffic.

questions.question: If your throttle gets stuck, what should you do?

options.text: Jump off the motorcycle.
Apply the brakes.
Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Do not try to twist the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: Try twisting the throttle back and forth to free it. If this does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch right away.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use hard pressure on the front brake to stop the front tire from locking.
Use only the rear brake.
Use one brake at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes on slippery surfaces to slow down. Squeeze the front brake slowly to avoid locking the front wheel. Use gentle pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the center portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding close to the passing driver increases crash risk. Riding far from them may make them return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: Motorcycles are hard to see at night. What should a rider do about this?

options.text: Slow down when riding at night.
Honk your horn often when riding at night.
Do not ride at night.
Stay directly in front of another vehicle so their headlights show you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when riding at night.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, slow down, increase your following distance, use other vehicles' headlights to see ahead, use your high beam (unless near other vehicles), and be ready to change your lane position.

questions.question: What happens when you brake while turning?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
It works the same as braking on a straight road.
You gain more traction as you lean into the curve.
You may lose traction as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may lose traction as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but it requires care. When leaning, some tire grip is used for turning. This means less grip is available for stopping.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They happen at speeds above 35 mph.
They happen at night.
They are caused by worn tires.
They involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders who have had the motorcycle for less than six months.

questions.question: Your rear wheel locks up while braking on dry pavement. What should you do?

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then press it again quickly.
Release the rear brake and shift down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel if it is upright and moving in a straight line.
